method: All successful-repeat raw samples pooled without outlier removal; nearest-rank P95/P99; inverse mean throughput excludes 210ms pacing sleeps. Failed repeats are preserved and disable headline ratios for that case.
caveats: GitHub workflow success does not mean every benchmark repeat succeeded: one zsys cold_basic repeat rejected a partial scan and remains a recorded failure.
Network and full metadata parity passed. Full has exactly 163 observed PIDs in both implementations and the same three mounts.
The directory scaling/100 contains actual 164-PID samples because the runner already exceeded the requested 100-PID target; it is not a 100-PID result.

Scaling 500 and 1000 have exactly matched counts. Scaling 5000 and 10000 ran successfully, but background process churn caused unequal count ranges, so no cross-library ratio is claimed at those scales.
Main basic has different process-count ranges and no ratio is claimed. cpu_hot and basic_hot have mismatched CPU freshness and no ratio is claimed.
Tiny nonzero allocations in zsys process/full results reflect observed changes during a real runner workload; only stable collector paths can be called allocation-free.
Requested Rust allocation bytes exclude allocator metadata and allocations made directly by native C libraries. VmHWM includes the executable, harness, allocator, and all process memory.
Cold cases measure collector construction, first refresh, and destruction with OS caches warm; they are not machine cold boot or page-cache eviction tests.
A shared hosted runner is not dedicated controlled hardware. These descriptive distributions do not establish universal latency or statistical confidence intervals.
